Volume 16 · Chapter 05

Question design and identification strategy

Research Author-reviewed · Prerequisites: v16-c04

By the endFormulate a research question with an explicit path from data or assumptions to conclusions.

Turn a question into an argument that could fail

Capability. Formulate a research question with an explicit path from observations or assumptions to a conclusion. The prerequisite is referee reports and research judgment. Bring the distinction between a claim's importance and the evidence that supports it. The agenda contract and literature map tell you why a question matters; this chapter specifies exactly what would answer it. The primary setting is macro-finance, supported by financial econometrics. All institutions, assignments and numbers in the two worked cases are fictional teaching constructions.

A promising question has an object, an economic reason to care about it, and a possible route to an answer. “Does finance matter?” has no defined contrast. “What is the coefficient on funding?” names a statistic without saying what it means. A stronger question names an intervention or comparison, a population, an outcome and a horizon, then exposes the assumptions connecting that target to observable evidence. A well-designed study can still find no effect or remain inconclusive. Design quality cannot be defined by obtaining the favored conclusion.

This chapter produces a design contract: a written commitment linking the question, target, counterfactual, measurement, comparison, assumptions, diagnostic evidence, feasibility and claim boundary. It is a thinking device, not an enforceable legal agreement or a completed preregistration. Later chapters develop theory, data ethics, power and analysis plans. Here the purpose is to prevent an undefined or unidentified question from being concealed by additional computation.

1. Separate the target, the estimator and the mechanism

An estimand is the quantity you want to know, specified before choosing a convenient regression. A statistic is a function of observed data; an estimator is a rule for using that statistic to learn the target. An estimate is its realized value. Identification asks whether the permitted data distribution and maintained assumptions determine the target, even before finite-sample uncertainty. More observations can improve precision without resolving identification. Conversely, an identified target can be estimated poorly with little information.

For an intervention, write Yi(1) and Yi(0) for the outcome unit i would have under the two specified alternatives. The unobserved alternative is a counterfactual; it is not automatically the observed outcome of a different unit. Define whether the target averages over eligible units, treated units, a subgroup or a different population to which you hope to transport the result. Specify equal versus size weights, the time horizon and the units. An average bank effect in millions of currency is neither a percentage elasticity nor an aggregate investment effect.

The intervention must be concrete enough that its alternatives are interpretable. An offer of access, actual borrowing and the amount borrowed are different treatments. “No early offer during the first ninety days, followed by normal eligibility” differs from permanent exclusion. If banks respond to each other's assignments, write potential outcomes as Yi(zi,z−i) and define an exposure or assignment-policy contrast; writing Yi(zi) alone does not remove the interaction. An aggregate policy question may require that richer target.

A mechanism explains the intermediate steps linking the intervention to the outcome. Early refinancing access might change available cash, the price of funds, perceived safety or lending terms; customers may then change borrowing. An effect of an offer does not by itself distinguish those channels. Observing a mediator after treatment does not make it an independently assigned treatment. Conditioning on it can select units whose uptake reflects unmeasured demand or risk. Keep the total-effect question separate from the mechanism question unless the design supplies the additional variation and assumptions needed for both.

A useful sentence sequence is: “I seek quantity T. I observe O. Under restrictions A, O determines T by argument G. If restriction A1 fails, explanation H can produce O with a different T. Evidence E would diagnose part of that failure; it would not prove every restriction.” If you cannot complete G, do not substitute the name of an estimator. If H cannot be described, you may not yet understand what the design excludes.

2. Make every inference bridge visible

Start with a mechanism sketch that includes competing paths. Then decide which question is actually feasible. For bank funding, draw the intended path from funding access to resources, lending decisions and borrower outcomes. Add paths from borrower demand, bank risk and policy selection to both observed funding and lending. Add feedback if lending opportunities influence funding choices. The drawing organizes the argument; its arrows are maintained causal claims, not facts discovered by the diagram.

Next choose the counterfactual comparison. Random assignment can justify a difference in offer-group means for an offer effect, given the defined assignment, outcome and interference conditions. An observational before–after comparison needs an argument about what would otherwise have changed. A within-borrower comparison can remove a common borrower component but still require a restriction on relationship-specific demand. The Khwaja–Mian draft inspected in Chapter 2 is a bounded conceptual connection for the distinction between lending at an affected bank and a borrower's ability to replace credit; its selected method passages also discuss bank-specific demand. That connection does not certify the fictional designs below or transfer a published estimate to them.

Write the identifying assumption in words and symbols where useful. State the population over which it holds, the timing, and whether it is an assignment fact, a measurement convention or an untestable restriction. Then write a threat–evidence–consequence row for each major vulnerability. A placebo may contradict an implication of the design; passing it may leave the relevant post-period counterfactual unrestricted. A control variable is useful only with a defensible role and timing. Adding every recorded variable can change the target or condition on consequences of treatment.

Finally ask whether the required observations can exist in usable form. Access permission, stable identifiers, treatment records, coverage of exits, comparable units and an auditable outcome are part of the design. A sophisticated comparison is unavailable if the files cannot implement it. State a stop or pivot rule before observing the main result: stop causal estimation when the assignment record cannot be recovered, or narrow the outcome when its definition cannot be reconciled. Do not make “the effect is significant” an access or measurement gate.

Worked case 1. A complete contract for an early-refinancing offer

Question and significance. A fictional research team asks: “Among the eligible banks in a specified pilot, what is the mean effect of receiving an early-refinancing offer on net new lending during the next ninety days?” The economic uncertainty is whether an access policy changes lending at participating institutions. It is narrower than asking whether refinancing raises national investment. The committee has not run this pilot. Everything below is a completed proposed design and a synthetic demonstration of its inference, not an observed policy result or permission to conduct an intervention.

Completed design contract A
ElementCommitted specification
Population and unitThe fixed roster of eligible banks defined before assignment. Equal weight per bank; no selection by later take-up or survival. The demonstration has four banks A–D.
Intervention and comparatorZ=1 is the documented early offer at date 0, with terms fixed in advance; Z=0 is no early offer during the ninety-day window. Ordinary eligibility after that window is the same. Assignment is an offer, not a forced loan.
Outcome and timingY is cumulative cash advances to borrowers minus principal repayments over those ninety days, in millions of a fixed currency. Loan sales, write-offs and valuation changes are separately reconciled rather than counted as new advances. A negative net flow is permitted.
TargetThe eligible-roster average offer effect T=(1/N)Σ[Yi(1)−Yi(0)]. This is an intention-to-treat target: non-takers remain in their assigned offer group.
Assignment and comparisonChoose exactly half the roster uniformly at random for the offer. For the four-bank demonstration, every two-bank subset has probability 1/6. Estimate T by offered mean Y minus unoffered mean Y.
Identifying restrictionsAssignment follows the recorded lottery; outcomes correspond to the specified offers; all assigned units' outcomes are measured consistently; and, for this individual-offer target, other banks' offers do not affect a bank's outcome. No claim that these conditions hold in an actual banking market is supplied.
Mechanism and claim ceilingAccess may change resources or funding terms and then lending. The primary result concerns the offer package at these banks; it is not a per-unit effect of actual refinancing, an identified mediator effect, a borrower total-credit effect or a welfare result.

Why this comparison addresses the target. In a fixed even roster with n=N/2 offered banks, the estimated offered mean is ΣZiYi(1)/n. Each bank is offered with probability n/N, so its expectation is the roster mean of Y(1). The same argument for (1−Zi)Yi(0)/(N−n) gives the roster mean of Y(0). Subtracting gives T. This is a design expectation over the specified lottery, conditional on the full potential-outcome schedule. It does not say every assignment yields T, that outcomes for the same bank are both observable, or that the estimate's uncertainty is zero. Interference or selective missing outcomes would break the argument as written.

Synthetic full schedule. The following potential outcomes are supplied solely so the argument can be checked. A real pilot observes one potential outcome per bank. Ordered A,B,C,D, the no-offer values are (8,10,12,14) and offer values are (10,14,18,18). Effects are (2,4,6,4) million each; their mean is 4 million. With A and C offered, the observed offered mean is 14 and the unoffered mean is 12; the estimate is 2 million. A realized estimate different from four is not evidence that randomization failed.

All possible assignments in the four-bank teaching schedule
Offered pairOffered meanUnoffered meanDifference
AB1213−1
AC14122
AD14113
BC16115
BD16106
CD1899

The ordered contrasts are (-1,2,3,5,6,9), whose mean is 4. This enumeration is possible because the teaching schedule reveals all outcomes; it is not a procedure for recovering all missing potential outcomes from the realized pilot. No p-value, confidence interval or claim of adequate pilot power follows from the displayed mean alone. Those require a separately specified inferential question and procedure.

Completed alternative-explanation register. An association between take-up and lending could reflect selection of banks with better loan opportunities. Retaining assignment as treatment avoids that particular reinterpretation; it does not identify the effect of take-up. A direct signal from the offer could change customer confidence even when no refinancing is used. That is part of the offer's total effect, but an alternative to the cash-resource mechanism. Borrower switching between offered and unoffered banks could change control outcomes, violating the no-interference restriction. A separate exposure mapping and assignment-policy target would then be needed; controlling for post-offer borrower switching does not repair the original argument automatically.

Completed threat, diagnostic and decision record
ThreatEvidence soughtConsequence and limit
Allocation was altered after the drawPreserved eligibility list, randomization record, offer timestamps and all overrides.Analyze assignment as actually implemented only if its probabilities and interpretation are defensible; otherwise withdraw the lottery-based causal claim. Baseline balance alone cannot reconstruct a missing assignment process.
Lending flow is confused with a stock changeTransaction categories and a reconciliation of advances, repayments, sales, write-offs and valuation changes.Stop this outcome analysis if components cannot be distinguished. A different descriptive stock outcome needs its own contract.
Exit, merger or reporting loss follows the offerTrack the original roster and its outcome perimeter, retain pre-exit activity and obtain an auditable mapping for reorganizations.Do not drop units or replace unobserved flows with zero. If comparable complete outcomes cannot be recovered, document missingness and revise identification rather than reporting a survivor effect as the roster effect.
Cross-bank spillovers are economically materialPermitted borrower-link and substitution information, institutional interviews and the actual allocation scale.If the single-bank counterfactual is implausible, redesign the assignment or define a policy-level effect with explicit exposure. A small measured spillover in one proxy does not prove none exists.

Completed feasibility and decision contract. Before any real launch, obtain the applicable institutional and ethics approvals, confirm authority and capacity to administer the offer, establish permitted access to assignment and transaction records, and pilot the outcome reconciliation without using treatment results to select a preferred outcome. These are project-specific requirements to establish, not claims that approval has been obtained. A named design lead owns the assignment audit; a data lead owns the roster and measurement crosswalk; an independent reviewer challenges the interference and outcome arguments. Stop the proposed causal study if allocation records or comparable outcomes cannot be supplied. If only usable bank statements remain, return to a clearly labeled descriptive stock comparison. A zero, negative or imprecise offer-effect estimate is retained under the same reporting rule.

Completed conclusion template. “The proposed design targets a ninety-day eligible-bank offer effect on net lending flows under a recorded lottery, complete comparable outcomes and no cross-bank interference. The synthetic schedule illustrates unbiasedness over assignments, not an empirical effect. Mechanism, total borrower credit, aggregate investment, welfare and transport beyond the eligible roster require separate evidence.” This sentence preserves a meaningful causal question while exposing exactly where it could fail.

3. Test whether another explanation fits the same observations

When assignment is observational, ask for two complete stories that fit the evidence. If they imply different target effects while satisfying all restrictions you have actually defended, the target is not identified. The response is not necessarily to abandon the topic: obtain distinguishing evidence, justify an additional restriction, report an identified set, or ask a descriptive question. What is unacceptable is choosing the favorable story while describing it as compelled by the data.

Sensitivity analysis makes an otherwise hidden restriction explicit. A sensitivity interval for an unobserved departure is not a sampling confidence interval or a probability distribution. Rambachan and Roth's inspected discussion of restricted departures from parallel trends provides conceptual context for this distinction. The elementary two-group construction below is original and is not their estimator, confidence-set procedure or a demonstration of its coverage. A plausible numerical range requires substantive defense; writing a small range does not make the effect well established.

Worked case 2. An observational proposal with an explicit failure and repair

Question and target. Another fictional team has comparable loan-stock records but no randomized offer. It asks: “For banks exposed to a specified date-1 funding disruption, what was the average effect of that disruption on their date-1 loan stock?” The target is the exposed-group average treatment effect at date 1, in millions of the same currency. Exposure is fixed from documented pre-event funding arrangements, not from the subsequent loan decline. This timing prevents a circular definition but does not make exposure randomly assigned.

The design fixes a baseline bank roster, stable accounting perimeter and equal bank weights. Both groups are untreated at dates −1 and 0; exposed banks encounter the disruption between dates 0 and 1, and comparison banks do not. Initially assume no anticipation, comparable complete measurement and no effect on the comparison group. These restrictions concern this proposed contrast and must be defended. Banks exiting the file remain part of the target; missing stocks are not assumed to be zero, and a merger requires a documented perimeter mapping. If that mapping is unavailable, the declared target is not measured.

Original observed group means, in millions; the groups have equal fixed size
GroupDate −1Date 0Date 1
Exposed E404034
Comparison C404038

The two histories are (40,40,34,40,40,38), ordered E then C. Observed changes are −6 and −2, giving the difference in changes -4. Denote the exposed-group effect by τ=E[Y1(1)−Y1(0)|E]. Let b=E[Y1(0)−Y0(0)|E]−E[Y1(0)−Y0(0)|C] be the otherwise-unobserved difference in untreated trends. No anticipation identifies observed date-0 outcomes with untreated ones; unaffected controls identify their observed date-1 outcome with Y1(0). Adding and subtracting E[Y1(0)|E] gives the exact identity D=τ+b. Thus τ=D−b. Setting b=0 is the parallel-untreated-trends restriction; it is not a property of the subtraction itself.

Two complete counterfactual explanations. In World A, exposed banks would have ended at 38 without the disruption; their untreated change would equal the comparison group's −2. Their observed 34 implies τ=−4 and b=0. In World B, exposed banks would have ended at 34 even without disruption because their customers' demand declined more after date 0. Then τ=0 and b=−4. Both worlds have exactly the displayed histories, including identical changes before date 0, no anticipation and unaffected controls. Their ordered (untreated exposed endpoint,τ,b) values are ((38,-4,0),(34,0,-4)). Repeating the same histories for more banks would not distinguish them. Equal pre-event means and trends cannot logically determine an unobserved post-event untreated trend.

Completed identification repair. Suppose a substantive argument supports b∈[−1,2] million: absent the disruption, the exposed group's mean change would have been at most one million worse or two million better than the comparison group's. This is an added maintained bound, not information in the table. Then (-1,2) implies τ∈(-6,-3), because D=−4. The endpoints are attained at (τ,b)=(−6,2) and (−3,−1). Every intermediate τ is compatible: choose b=−4−τ and untreated exposed endpoint 34−τ, which lies between 37 and 40. Keep every observed cell fixed. The set is therefore sharp within this stated mean model and bound, without claiming sampling coverage. World B is excluded by the bound; the bound must be defended rather than justified by its exclusion of that unwelcome world.

Completed design contract B
ElementCommitted specification and decision
MechanismThe disruption may limit bank funding and then loan supply. Borrower demand, bank risk and anticipated opportunities can also influence pre-event funding arrangements and later loan stocks. Stock changes additionally include repayments, write-offs and other measured accounting components.
Primary comparisonDifference in changes for the fixed exposed and comparison rosters. Report D as descriptive without a causal restriction. Report τ=D only under b=0; under the defended interval report the full effect set and its dependence on that interval.
Distinguishing evidenceInspect the event and exposure assignment, prior borrower-sector composition, contemporaneous demand information and accounting components. Seek evidence specifically relevant to whether untreated exposed trends could diverge. Do not use the observed lending decline to define exposure.
Diagnostics and their limitsPre-event trends can reveal some inconsistencies or motivate wider bounds, but the two worlds show that a passed pretrend check cannot prove b=0. A comparison outcome plausibly unaffected by funding but exposed to the same demand forces could be informative only after defending those two properties.
Feasibility gateProceed only with auditable pre-event exposure, complete comparable roster outcomes and evidence sufficient to argue for the chosen comparison. If records support the table but not the causal restriction, deliver the observed comparison, alternative worlds and a sensitivity map with conditional claims.
Claim boundaryBank loan stocks over this event window, not new credit flows, the cash-resource mechanism, borrower total credit, investment or welfare. The bound describes identification uncertainty and must be kept separate from any subsequent sampling uncertainty.

A second bridge: from a bank's loan to a borrower's credit. Even a valid causal lending effect does not mechanically answer the aggregate question. Consider an original accounting illustration for one borrower, not an estimate of the group's causal response. The borrower owes lender A 40, lender B 20 and lender C zero at date 0; at date 1 the corresponding stocks are 34,22,4. All records are comparable, and the zero at C is verified absence of a loan rather than a missing observation. Ordered (A0,B0,C0,A1,B1,C1), inputs are (40,20,0,34,22,4). The changes by lender are (-6,2,4); total credit is (60,60). A's six-million contraction is replaced within this ledger. Restricting the file to baseline lenders A and B yields totals (60,56) and a misleading four-million contraction if labeled total credit.

To ask a borrower-total-credit question, redefine the population as the baseline borrower roster, include new as well as old lenders within a declared credit universe, and specify what treatment a borrower receives when several lenders have different exposure. A complete bank-credit registry would still omit informal or nonbank credit unless included by design; the target must say so. The ledger establishes an accounting possibility, not that real borrowers always replace lost credit or that their investment is unchanged. A causal estimate for the revised borrower target needs a new comparison and assumptions. Simply adding up a partial relationship sample does not supply them.

Completed decision memo. “Our observed comparison is −4 million in bank loan stocks. The supplied histories permit both a −4-million effect and a zero effect. With the additional b∈[−1,2] restriction, the effect set is [−6,−3]; the restriction, rather than the pretrend match, delivers its negative sign. We will first audit exposure, accounting and demand evidence. Until a counterfactual restriction is defensible, the deliverable is a descriptive comparison and an explicit sensitivity analysis. We will not label the bank outcome borrower credit or investment. A borrower-level extension requires new-lender coverage and a new identification contract.” This is a reasoned project decision even if the desired point estimate never becomes defensible.

4. Choose the smallest claim that resolves the economic uncertainty

The two contracts answer different questions with different evidence. The offer design makes its assignment mechanism explicit and can identify a total offer effect in a defined population under its restrictions. It still cannot reveal an exclusive cash channel or aggregate welfare from that estimate alone. The observational design makes the missing untreated trend visible and shows exactly what an added restriction buys. A narrower conditional conclusion can be economically useful if the uncertainty it resolves matters and the restriction is defensible.

Before committing resources, hold a design review in which someone argues the strongest rival explanation. Require a response tied to information, not a longer list of regressions. Write one row for the empirical target, one for any mechanism target and one for any policy target; do not merge their assumptions. State what result would alter the interpretation in each row. Preserving an exploratory change in a versioned memo is legitimate learning; silently revising the original target after viewing results is a different practice.

The output of this chapter is a question contract and an identification argument, not a claim of novelty, adequate precision or authorization. Carry the argument into theory building and model discipline: a model should explain why its restrictions matter and what observations could challenge them. Carry unresolved measurement, access and uncertainty requirements into the later data and design chapters. A method becomes part of a research contribution only when its assumptions and scope answer a substantive question the literature has left open.

5. Exercises

  1. A proposal asks, “Does refinancing improve the economy?” Rewrite it as the exact bank-level question in contract A. Specify population, treatment, comparator, outcome, horizon, weighting and estimand. Then state two bridges still needed to answer the original broad question.
  2. Use the four-bank full schedule. If B and D receive the offer, calculate the estimate and its difference from the target. Verify the mean across all six possible assignments. Explain which parts of this calculation a real pilot with only one observed assignment cannot perform from its observed outcomes alone.
  3. In a new synthetic mechanism example, Z is a randomized offer, M is actual refinancing uptake and observed M=Z. In World R, Y=10+4M. In World S, Y=10+4Z and M has no causal effect. For Z=0 and Z=1 give observed (Z,M,Y) in both worlds. Then hold Z=1 while intervening to set M=0 and compare Y. What can the offer contrast identify, and what additional evidence would a mechanism claim need?
  4. Using contract B's observed histories, construct a third world with a positive effect τ=2. Give the unobserved exposed date-1 outcome, its untreated trend, b and the check D=τ+b. Explain whether more repetitions of the same observed table or its flat pretrend rule out this world.
  5. An institutional reviewer argues that b may lie in [−5,2] instead of [−1,2]. Derive the sharp effect set, give compatible endpoint worlds and test whether zero and a positive effect are possible. State what this change does and does not imply about sampling uncertainty.
  6. Using the borrower ledger, compute the apparent change from lender A only, baseline lenders only and the complete three-lender universe. Define a borrower-level total bank-credit target that includes newly appearing lenders. Explain why even the complete ledger is insufficient to identify an effect on investment.
  7. The offer project has transaction data only for banks still reporting at day ninety; the observational project has matched loan stocks but cannot recover pre-event funding exposure. Write a stop or pivot decision for each, identify what missing evidence would permit reconsideration, and propose one targeted diagnostic with its limitation. Do not repair either problem by replacing missing values with zero.
  8. Write a complete design-review memo choosing one of the two projects as a first paper under the following constraint: no new intervention is authorized, but contract B's comparable histories and permitted accounting records are available. Include an economically meaningful question, feasible deliverable, estimand or descriptive target, identifying boundary, strongest alternative explanation, next information request and a result-independent stop or pivot rule.
Complete solutions and evaluation criteria

1. Define the question before its ambition

“Among the fixed preassignment eligible bank roster, what is the equally weighted average effect of an early-refinancing offer at date 0, compared with no early offer during the window, on cumulative borrower advances minus principal repayments over the next ninety days, in millions of the fixed currency?” The target is N−1Σ[Yi(1)−Yi(0)], with assignment defining treatment whether or not funds are taken. A broad economic conclusion additionally requires a bridge from bank flows to borrowers' total financing and real investment, and a welfare/aggregation argument accounting for costs, substitution and spillovers. Credit all seven specification elements plus two concrete bridges; a title containing “causal” or a regression formula alone is insufficient.

2. An unbiased rule can give a different realization

B and D have offered mean (14+18)/2=16; A and C have no-offer mean (8+12)/2=10. The estimate is 6, exceeding the target four by 2. Across the six assignments the sum is −1+2+3+5+6+9=24, so the equally weighted mean is 4. A real pilot observes its realized group difference but not the full schedule, target effect or all six alternative estimates. The expectation result is an implication of the design and assumptions, not permission to fill missing potential outcomes with observed group means. No precision claim follows solely from unbiasedness.

3. Total-effect evidence need not isolate a mediator

Both worlds give ((0,0,10),(1,1,14)). The randomized offer contrast is 4. Under the hypothetical intervention Z=1,M=0, World R gives 10 while World S gives 14: (10,14). The observed joint distribution therefore cannot distinguish a refinancing channel from a direct offer channel in this construction. Evidence varying uptake independently of the direct offer channel, with a defensible intervention and relevant restrictions, could help; alternatively justify a substantive exclusion restriction and examine its implications. Simply controlling for M, which equals Z here, provides no separate variation. No claim that the required intervention is practical or authorized earns credit without evidence. The example does not refute an offer effect; it limits its mechanism interpretation.

4. A favorable observed effect can conceal a worse counterfactual

With observed exposed outcome 34 and τ=2, its no-disruption outcome must be 32. Its untreated change from 40 is −8, compared with −2 for controls, so b=−6. The ordered values (counterfactual endpoint,untreated change,b,τ+b) are (32,-8,-6,-4). All observed histories remain unchanged. The effect is beneficial relative to an even worse counterfactual while the observed stock falls. Repeating those observations adds no distinguishing information, and the common earlier flat trend imposes no logical restriction on this later untreated demand change. The original b∈[−1,2] restriction excludes this world; the observations alone do not.

5. A wider credible departure changes the conclusion

Since τ=−4−b, b∈[−5,2] gives (-6,1). At b=2 the untreated exposed endpoint is 40 and τ=−6; at b=−5 it is 33 and τ=1. Every intermediate pair preserves the observed34. Zero is possible at b=−4 with counterfactual34; a positive effect is possible for b<−4, including τ=1 at the lower bound. The sign is no longer identified under this wider restriction. This is a change in maintained identification information; it neither estimates a standard error nor assigns probabilities within the set. Sampling inference would have to account separately for how the observed group quantities are estimated.

6. Match the outcome to the credit universe

A alone changes by34−40=−6. Baseline lenders A+B change from60 to56, or−4. The complete stated universe A+B+C changes from60 to60, or0. The three changes are (-6,-4,0). A suitable descriptive target is the equally weighted mean change in each baseline borrower's total outstanding bank credit across all lenders in a fixed defined registry universe, including newly formed relationships, with zero distinguished from unobserved credit. A causal version additionally defines exposure and its counterfactual. Total credit remaining unchanged does not establish unchanged terms, maturity, investment demand, nonbank finance or investment; the ledger has no identified investment counterfactual or even an investment outcome. Full credit requires both complete coverage and the outcome/causality boundary.

7. Missing design evidence changes the claim

Offer project: pause the roster-level effect analysis and seek transaction histories for exited or nonreporting banks plus mappings for reorganizations; retain the original roster and missingness status. Comparing missing-outcome rates by randomized offer is a targeted diagnostic of differential reporting, but equal rates do not establish that missing outcomes are innocuous. Until recovery or a defended missingness analysis is possible, do not call a complete-case contrast the eligible-roster effect. Observational project: stop the intended exposure contrast because treatment cannot be classified from pre-event records. Seek timestamped funding arrangements or a validated historical exposure source. If unavailable, pivot to a clearly described accounting/coverage audit; do not classify exposure from the loan decline. Checking the consistency of recovered exposure across independent records could reveal error, but agreement of two copied records is not independent validation. Credit requires an actionable decision and missing-evidence request for each project plus a diagnostic whose limit is stated.

8. A complete constrained design memo

“Choose a first paper on the observed difference in loan-stock changes between the fixed groups in contract B, provided their pre-event exposure can be audited. The economic question is whether the proposed funding-transmission narrative is consistent with comparable accounting evidence, and what counterfactual restrictions would turn the description into an effect estimate. The feasible deliverable is a roster and accounting audit, the group comparison D, and explicit alternative explanations and sensitivity sets. We will not launch the unauthorized offer project or describe D as a causal effect without defending b. The strongest rival explanation is a post-event demand deterioration concentrated at exposed banks; its World B produces the same histories with no funding effect. Request permitted pre-event exposure documents, borrower-sector information and accounting components to assess this alternative. If exposure or comparable outcomes cannot be recovered, pivot to a measurement report; if those work but the causal restriction remains unsupported, retain the descriptive paper and conditional sensitivity analysis. No decision depends on whether D is negative or statistically significant. Novelty remains to be assessed against the closest literature, and borrower investment is outside the current claim.” Other coherent memos can earn full credit. Require the seven requested elements, an actual inference boundary and a feasible information request; do not award full credit to a list of headings without decisions.

6. Teach-back and delayed retention

Teach-back. Explain to an economist outside macro-finance why a clean observed comparison can fail to identify a mechanism, and why a matched pretrend can fail to identify a treatment effect. Use one complete alternative world from each relevant example. State an information change that would matter.

Teach-back answer guide

The offer/uptake example has identical observed (Z,M,Y) in a cash-mediated world and a direct-offer world, yet a controlled uptake intervention gives different outcomes. The observation identifies the total randomized offer contrast under its assumptions, not that mediator contrast. The observational bank histories fit untreated exposed endpoints38 or34, producing effects−4 or0 with identical earlier trends. A defensible intervention separating uptake from the direct path could address the first ambiguity; evidence supporting a restriction on differential untreated trends could narrow the second. Neither a larger copy of the same dataset nor merely adding controls supplies those arguments.

Delayed retention. After a week, without the worked tables, write a one-page design contract for a question in another field. Include an estimand or descriptive target, units, population, timing, mechanism, comparison, two rival explanations, evidence that would discriminate between them, one access/measurement gate and the strongest honest claim if the gate fails.

Criteria and illustrative complete contract

“Among a fixed roster of eligible trainees, study the equal-person average effect of a randomly assigned invitation to a tutoring session, compared with no invitation before the test, on a common test score measured one month later. Assignment is invitation, not attendance. Under documented assignment, comparable outcome collection and no cross-person interference, compare invitation-group means; retain nonattenders in their assigned groups. Learning from tutoring and motivation from receiving the invitation are distinct mechanisms. Differential test participation is another rival explanation for an observed complete-case difference. Seek outcome follow-up for the entire roster and evidence capable of separating attendance effects from direct motivation; simply comparing attenders with nonattenders would not do so. Confirm permission to use assignment and score records before collecting them. If common scores or a roster cannot be obtained, abandon this causal comparison and produce a measurement/access report with no achievement-effect claim.” Full credit requires all requested elements and ties the gate to a changed claim. This is a fictional proposed contract, not an approved study or a result about actual education.

Source boundary. Only the bounded conceptual connections linked above are inherited from inspected primary documents: the Khwaja–Mian forthcoming draft's selected method passages and Rambachan–Roth's physical pages1–12 on restricted departures and identified versus confidence sets. No new source-body inspection, empirical estimate, general inference procedure or final-draft equivalence is claimed here. All schedules, contracts, accounts, counterfactual worlds and exercise solutions are original teaching material.

Sources and further study

  • Asim Khwaja and Atif Mian — Tracing the Impact of Bank Liquidity Shocks: Evidence from an Emerging Market (author-hosted forthcoming-AER draft) — Evidence-table row and bounded method comparison.
  • A More Credible Approach to Parallel Trends — Reduced-form/departure decomposition, relative-increment versus curvature sensitivity, and the difference between identified and confidence sets. Compact fibers and original square sharpness are proved directly, as is a separate finite known-Gaussian projection.
